sentences.text: 2 This appeal is filed by the appellant-insurance company challenging the judgment and award dated 16.08.2021 passed in MV.C. No.959/2020 by the Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.), Channarayapatna, Hassan.

2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the parties.
3.
The appellant was respondent No.2 before the Tribunal and respondent Nos.1 to 3 were petitioner Nos.1 to 3 and respondent No.4 was respondent No.1.
Therefore, the rank of the parties before the Tribunal is retained for the sake of convenience.
4. The case of the petitioners before the Tribunal was that they filed a claim petition seeking compensation for the death of one Ratnamma, who died in the accident that occurred on 05.10.2019.
It is alleged that the deceased Ratnamma was the wife of petitioner No.1 and the mother of petitioner Nos.2 and 3.

It is further alleged that on 05.10.2019 at about 6 10 NC:
2024:KHC:27679 p.m., the deceased as a pillion rider along with her daughter (petitioner No.3) as rider were proceeding on Hero Duet bike bearing No.KA-04-JF-1632 near Dindgur village, on the left side of Chennarayapatna-Nuggehalli main road.
At that time, respondent No.1-the driver of Tata Indica car bearing No.KA- 01-MC-5780 came from Chennarayapatna in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the petitioner's bike.
As a result, the deceased sustained grievous injuries on her head, chest and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
Hence, the petitioners filed the claim petition seeking compensation.
5. On the issuance of notice, respondent No.1-owner of the offending vehicle did not appear and he was placed ex- parte.
Respondent No.2-the insurer of the offending vehicle filed statement of objections denying the accident, age and income of the deceased.
The dependency of the petitioners on the deceased was also denied.
6. The Tribunal accordingly framed three issues.

In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 was examined as P.W.1 and marked exhibits P.1 to P.4 and on the side of NC: 2024:KHC:27679 respondents, no evidence was led nor any documents were marked.

7. The Tribunal considering the age of the deceased as 55 years took the notional income of the deceased as 14,000/- per month, since the accident was of the year 2019 and 10% towards future prospects and granted Rs.13,55,244/- towards loss of dependency.
The Tribunal also granted Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.1,20,000/- towards loss of consortium.
In all, it granted the compensation of Rs.15,05,244/- along with interest at 9% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The said award is challenged by the appellant-insurance company in this appeal.
8. The learned counsel for the appellant-insurance company has contended that the petitioner-claimant Nos.2 and 3 are major children.
Therefore, that cannot be considered as dependents for loss of dependency.
Petitioner No.1, husband also cannot be considered as dependent on his wife.
Therefore, 50% of income of the deceased should have been deducted towards personal expenses.
The learned counsel has also NC: 2024:KHC:27679 contended that the interest awarded on the compensation at 9% per annum should be reduced as it is on the higher side.
Accordingly, prayed for following the appeal.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for respondent-petitioners (claimants) objected the appeal and supported the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
10. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties, perused the records.

11. The point that arise for consideration in this appeal is :
(i) Whether the Tribunal is justified in awarding the compensation by treating the petitioners as dependents and deducting one-third of income towards personal expenses of the deceased ?
12.
On perusal of the records, it reveals that the accident in question, the death of the deceased in the accident, the age of the deceased in the accident are not in dispute.

The Tribunal NC:
2024:KHC:27679 has considered the notional income of the deceased at Rs.14000 per month depending on the age of the deceased, is also not in dispute.

13. The Tribunal has taken 10% of income future prospects, which comes to Rs.15400/-
[Rs.14,000+1400(10%)] and by deducting one-third of income towards personal expenses, it has awarded the compensation towards loss of dependency, which is under challenge.

14. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others Vs.Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in AIR 2009 SUPREME COURT 3104 has held that for a married person, one-third of income shall be deducted and for a bachelor, 50% should be deducted towards personal expenses.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others Vs.Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in AIR 2009 SUPREME COURT 3104
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further held that, if the petitioners are more than 3 in number, one-fourth of income should be deducted and if they are more than 4 in number, one-fifth should be deducted.
The same has been upheld by the Larger Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi's case and therefore, deducting 50% of income for a married person, NC: 2024:KHC:27679 cannot be acceptable.
Whether the petitioners are the husband and the major children, that is immaterial, but for a married person one-third of income should be deducted towards personal expenses.

Therefore,
taking one-third of income towards personal expenses of the deceased by the Tribunal cannot be found fault with.
Therefore, I answer the point in favour of the petitioners-claimants and against the appellant- insurance company.
15. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the remaining heads is just and reasonable and I do not find any error in the said award.

16. However, the Tribunal has awarded the interest at 9% per annum on the compensation, but looking to the facts, the award of interest at 9% per annum awarded on the compensation is to be reduced to 6% per annum.

17. In the result, I pass the following:

(ii) The compensation of Rs.15,05,244/- awarded by the Tribunal is confirmed.
However, the said compensation shall carry interest at 6% per annum instead of 9% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

(iii) The appellant insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation with interest at 6%
per annum, within two months from the date of receipt of a copy of the award.
(iv) The amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the Tribunal.
